image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on dark water. The duck features a glossy iridescent green head, a distinct white neck ring, a chestnut-brown breast, and a greyish-white body with black tail feathers. One orange webbed foot is visible paddling underwater. The background consists of calm, dark water with slight ripples.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellow-green in color, matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is streamlined and sits low in the water, indicating buoyancy. The plumage texture appears dense and smooth, typical of waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey/white body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One orange leg/foot is visible underwater. It shows the characteristic webbing between toes. The position is set back, appropriate for a swimming bird.
The folded wing structure is visible along the side, appearing broad and tapering towards the tail, consistent with avian anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short, and the characteristic upward curl of the central black tail feathers (sexually dimorphic trait of mallard drakes) is clearly visible.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the submerged orange foot and the water. AI often struggles with semi-transparent objects underwater. Also, verify if the iridescence on the green head looks like natural structural coloration or a flat, painted gradient.
